'''Jordan Tyler McRae''' (born March 28, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[ASK Karditsa B.C.|Karditsa]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|University of Tennessee Volunteers]], with whom he was twice First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]]. McRae was drafted 58th overall in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[San Antonio Spurs]], but never appeared in an [[NBA]] game for them, and won an [[2016 NBA Finals|NBA championship]] with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in 2016. He is a {{convert|1.96|m|ftin|sp=us}} tall [[shooting guard]]-[[small forward]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=007996&seasoncode=E2017#!careerstats MCRAE, JORDAN FORWARD HEIGHT: 1.98.]</ref>

McRae formerly held the [[NBA G League]] single-game scoring record (61 points). After spending time in the [[NBA G League]] and overseas, he signed with the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2018, and then in 2020 with the [[Detroit Pistons]], his most recent [[NBA]] team.

==High school career==
McRae attended [[Liberty County High School (Fleming, Georgia)|Liberty County High School]] in [[Hinesville, Georgia]], where he led the Panthers to multiple quarter-finals appearances, while earning prestigious All-State honors and a nomination for the [[2010 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]. He played one of his greatest high school basketball games to cap off his career with Liberty County, recording 37 points, 13 rebounds, and 5 assists. As a senior in 2009–10, he averaged 24 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, and four blocks per game.<ref name="bio">{{Cite web |title=Jordan McRae Bio |url=http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jordan_mcrae_710947.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140311020849/http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jordan_mcrae_710947.html |archive-date=March 11, 2014 |access-date=July 9, 2014 |website=UTSports.com}}</ref>

McRae also played with the highly regarded Atlanta Celtics in the [[Amateur Athletic Union]], which had previously been led by [[Josh Smith]] and [[Jordan Adams (basketball, born 1994)|Jordan Adams]].<ref name="bio" />

Considered a [[four-star recruit]] by [[Rivals.com]], McRae was listed as the No. 10 [[shooting guard]] and the No. 38 player in the nation in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jordan McRae Recruiting Profile |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/58248/jordan-mcrae |access-date=September 27, 2015 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Jordan McRae.jpg|thumb|right|McRae with the Tennessee Volunteers in 2014]]
After appearing in just 10 games as a freshman for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|University of Tennessee Volunteers]], McRae played in all 34 games as a sophomore in 2011–12 while earning 15 starting assignments. He also boosted his points per game average from 1.8 as a freshman to 8.6 as a sophomore as he was one of the SEC's top sixth men in 2011–12, coming off the bench to score in double figures in six of UT's last 14 games.<ref name="bio" />

As a junior in the 2012–13 season, McRae appeared in all 33 games with 22 starts as he finished the season as Tennessee's team leader in scoring (15.7 ppg; 4th in the SEC), minutes played (33.6 mpg), three-pointers made (60) and attempted (169), and three-point percentage (.355).<ref name=ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jordan-mcrae-1.html  "Jordan McRae,"] sports-reference.com.</ref> He also ranked second in assists (2.0 apg), blocks (0.9 bpg), and steals (0.8 spg) while earning first-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] and first-team [[ USBWA]] All-District IV honors.<ref name="bio" />

As a senior in the 2013–14 season, McRae started all 37 games while averaging 18.7 points (4th in the SEC), 3.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists, and 1.0 steals per game as he earned first-team All-SEC and second-team [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] Division I All-District 21 honors. <ref name=ref/>During Tennessee's four [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]] games, he led the team in scoring (19.8 ppg) and blocks (1.5 bpg) while also averaging 3.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game.<ref name="bio" />

In his four-year career at [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]], McRae played 114 games (74 starts) while averaging 13.3 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 1.8 assists in 27.1 minutes per game while shooting 41.7 percent from the floor.<ref name="bio" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jordan McRae College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jordan-mcrae-1.html |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Melbourne United (2014–2015)===
On June 26, 2014, McRae was selected with the 58th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. He was later traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on draft night, and went on to join the team for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 27, 2014 |title=Sixers Acquire Draft Rights To Jordan McRae From San Antonio Spurs |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140626-mcrae-trade |access-date=July 9, 2014 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=July 7, 2014 |title=Sixers Announce Samsung NBA Summer League Camp Invitees |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140707-vegas-camp-invitees |access-date=July 9, 2014 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> In four summer league games, he averaged 21.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, 1.0 assists, and 1.8 steals per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 Summer League Player Profile – Jordan McRae |url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2014/players/sl_jordan_mcrae/ |access-date=December 24, 2014 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

|website=FoxSportsPulse.com}}</ref>

===Delaware 87ers (2015–2016)===
On March 5, 2015, McRae was acquired by the [[Delaware 87ers]], the 76ers' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 5, 2015 |title=87ers acquire Jordan McRae |url=http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/87ers-acquire-jordan-mcrae/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304061648/http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/87ers-acquire-jordan-mcrae/ |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=March 5, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He made his debut for the 87ers the following day, recording 5 points, 4 rebounds, and 4 assists as a starter in a 123–112 win over the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 6, 2015 |title=Fort Wayne Mad Ants @ Delaware 87ers |url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20150306/FWNDEL/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160528175911/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20150306/FWNDEL/ |archive-date=May 28, 2016 |access-date=September 27, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On March 22, he recorded career-highs with 39 points and 13 rebounds in a 124–120 overtime loss to the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 22, 2015 |title=McRae shines in 124–120 overtime loss to Oklahoma City |url=http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/mcrae-shines-in-124-120-overtime-loss-to-oklahoma-city/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304073506/http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/mcrae-shines-in-124-120-overtime-loss-to-oklahoma-city/ |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=September 27, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>  For the 2015-16 season, in 13 games he averaged 18.4 points, 3.8 assists, and 1.1 steals per game.<ref name=refe/>

In July 2015, McRae re-joined the Philadelphia 76ers for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]], where he averaged 12.5 points and 3.0 rebounds in four games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 11, 2015 |title=Las Vegas Summer League Roster & Schedule |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150711-vegas-info |access-date=September 27, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On September 27, 2015, he signed with the 76ers,<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 27, 2015 |title=SIXERS ANNOUNCE 2015 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-announce-2015-training-camp-roster |access-date=September 27, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> only to be waived by the team on October 26 after appearing in seven preseason games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 26, 2015 |title=PHILADELPHIA 76ERS WAIVE FIVE |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-waive-five |access-date=October 26, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On November 2, he was reacquired by the 87ers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 2, 2015 |title=87ers finalize training camp roster |url=http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/87ers-finalize-training-camp-roster/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105122138/http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/87ers-finalize-training-camp-roster/ |archive-date=November 5, 2015 |access-date=November 7, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2016)===

|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-jordan-mcrae |access-date=January 29, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He made his NBA debut later that night, recording 12 points, 4 assists, 2 rebounds and 1 steal in 25 minutes off the bench in a 102–84 loss to the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 29, 2016 |title=Anthony returns and Knicks hand Suns 13th straight road loss |website=NBA.com}}</ref> 

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2016–2017)===
On February 28, McRae signed a 10-day contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 28, 2016 |title=Cavs Sign Jordan McRae To 10-Day Contract |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/mcrae-10-day-160228 |access-date=February 28, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Later that day, he made his debut for the Cavaliers in a 113–99 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]], recording eight points and one rebound in seven minutes off the bench.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 28, 2016 |title=Smith calls out Cavs, LeBron sits for 113–99 loss at Wizards |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160228/CLEWAS/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160302045126/http://www.nba.com/games/20160228/CLEWAS/gameinfo.html |archive-date=March 2, 2016 |access-date=February 28, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On March 9, he signed a multi-year contract with the Cavaliers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 9, 2016 |title=Cavs Sign Jordan McRae To Multi-Year Contract |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/mcrae-signing-160309 |access-date=March 9, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On April 11, he was assigned to the [[Canton Charge]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 11, 2016 |title=Cavs Assign Jordan McRae to Canton Charge |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/mcrae-assign-160411 |access-date=April 11, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> for a day of training.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 11, 2016 |title=Cavs Recall Kaun and McRae |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/recall-kaun-mcrae-160411 |access-date=April 11, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He was reassigned to Canton the next day to help the team in Game 1 of the D-League Eastern Conference Finals against the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 12, 2016 |title=Cavaliers Assign Kaun and McRae to Canton Charge |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/kaun-mcrae-assign-160411 |access-date=April 12, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> 

The next day, McRae was recalled by the Cavaliers<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 13, 2016 |title=Cavs Recall Kaun and McRae – April 13, 2016 |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/recall-kaun-mcrae-160413 |access-date=April 13, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> and that night, he scored an NBA career-high 36 points, along with four rebounds and seven assists in 47 minutes, against the [[Detroit Pistons]], including a three-pointer to send the game into overtime. In overtime, he had a chance to tie it in the final second, but battling leg cramps, he missed two free throws after being fouled on a three-pointer.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 13, 2016 |title=LeBron sits as Pistons beat Cavaliers in playoff non-preview |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/DETCLE/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170114013327/http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/DETCLE/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 14, 2017 |access-date=April 13, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Cavaliers made it to the [[2016 NBA Finals]] where they defeated the [[Golden State Warriors]] 4–3. Despite the Cavaliers going down 3–1 in the series following a Game 4 loss, they went on to win the series in seven games to become the first team in NBA history to win the championship after being down 3–1.

On June 28, 2016, the Cavaliers exercised their 2016–17 team option on McRae's contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Haynes |first=Chris |date=June 28, 2016 |title=Sources: Cleveland Cavaliers to exercise team option on guard Jordan McRae |url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2016/06/cleveland_cavaliers_to_exercis.html |access-date=July 3, 2016 |website=Cleveland.com}}</ref> He later joined the Cavaliers for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]], where after averaging 24.3 points per game, he was named to the All-Summer League First Team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 18, 2016 |title=Wolves' Tyus Jones named 2016 Summer League MVP |url=http://www.nba.com/2016/news/07/18/2016-all-summer-league-team/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160720191756/http://www.nba.com/2016/news/07/18/2016-all-summer-league-team/index.html |archive-date=July 20, 2016 |access-date=July 18, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On December 31, 2016, McRae made his first start of the season in place of the injured [[Kyrie Irving]] and scored a season-high 20 points in a 121–109 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 31, 2016 |title=James, Love help Cavs end 2016 with 121–109 win over Hornets |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899947 |access-date=December 31, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On March 1, 2017, McRae was waived by the Cavaliers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 1, 2017 |title=Cavaliers Waive Jordan McRae |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/waive-mcrae-170301 |access-date=March 1, 2017 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> With Cleveland and Phoenix combined, in 2015-16 in 22 games he averaged 8.9 minutes, 4.5 points, and 1.1 assists, per game while shooting .455 from three-point range.<ref name="basketball.realgm.com" />>

===Baskonia (2017)===
On August 20, 2017, McRae signed a one-year deal with [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 20, 2017 |title=Baskonia adds scorer McRae |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/853mvim7dluptesx |access-date=August 20, 2017 |work=EuroLeague.net |language=en}}</ref> On January 6, 2018, McRae parted ways with Baskonia. He underwent surgery on his left shoulder in [[Vitoria-Gasteiz]] and was expected to be sidelined for five more months, missing the remainder of the season. He was first injured on September 15 and was only able to play four games. He took part in four [[EuroLeague]] games, averaging five points, 1.0 assists, 1.0 steals, and three fouls drawn per game.<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 7, 2018 |title=Baskonia, McRae, part ways |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8g9wqo7f7tfw8ni9 |access-date=January 7, 2018 |work=EuroLeague.net |language=en}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2018–2020)===
[[File:Jordan McRae 2020.jpg|thumb|right|McRae in 2020]]
On September 20, 2018, the [[Washington Wizards]] announced that they had signed McRae to a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Capital City Go-Go]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref name="Wizards-Training-Camp">{{Cite web |date=September 20, 2018 |title=Wizards announce 2018 Training Camp roster and schedule |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-announce-2018-training-camp-roster-and-schedule |access-date=September 20, 2018 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> 

On January 18, 2019, McRae set a new NBA G League season-high with 54 points in a win against the [[Maine Red Claws]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 19, 2019 |title=Jordan McRae: Sets G League scoring mark for 2018–19 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jordan-mcrae-sets-g-league-scoring-mark-for-2018-19/ |access-date=January 19, 2019 |work=MelbourneUtd.com.au |publisher=cbssports.com}}</ref> In the G League, he averaged 30.4 points, 4.9 rebounds, 3.9 assists, and 1.6 steals per game, and shot .849 from the free throw line.<ref name="basketball.realgm.com">{{Cite web |title=Jordan McRae Player Profile, Detroit Pistons – RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jordan-McRae/Summary/9345}}</ref> On April 9, 2019, the [[Washington Wizards]] announced that they had converted McRae's [[two-way contract]] to a standard NBA contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 9, 2019 |title=Wizards sign Jordan McRae to standard NBA contract |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-jordan-mcrae-nba-contract-tarik-phillip |access-date=April 9, 2019 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> In the 2018-19 season in 27 games he averaged 12.3 minutes, 5.9 points, and 1.1 assists per game while shooting .800 from the free throw line.<ref name="basketball.realgm.com" />  In the 2019-20 season with Washington in 29 games he averaged 22.6 minutes, 12.8 points, 2.5 assists, and 0,7 steals per game.<ref name="basketball.realgm.com" />

===Denver Nuggets (2020)===
On February 6, 2020, McRae was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for [[Shabazz Napier]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 6, 2020 |title=Nuggets Acquire Jordan McRae |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-mcrae-020620 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> In the 2019-20 season with Denver in 4  games he averaged 8.0 minutes, 2.3 points, and 1.0 assist per game.<ref name="basketball.realgm.com" /> On March 1, 2020, McRae was waived by the Nuggets after a contract buyout agreement was reached.

===Detroit Pistons (2020)===
On March 4, 2020, the [[Detroit Pistons]] claimed McRae off waivers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 4, 2020 |title=Pistons claim Jordan McRae off waivers |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/03/04/pistons-claim-jordan-mcrae-waivers-0 |access-date=March 4, 2020 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> In the 2019-20 season with Detroit in 4  games he averaged 24.5 minutes, 11.8 points, and 1.8 assists per game.<ref name="basketball.realgm.com" /> On March 1, 2020, McRae was waived by the Nuggets after a contract buyout agreement was reached.

===Beijing Ducks (2020–2021)===
On December 27, 2020, McRae signed a contract with the [[Beijing Ducks]] worth $1.5M for 25 games.<ref>{{cite web | last=Kirschenbaum | first=Alex | title=Jordan McRae To Sign With Beijing Ducks | website=Hoops Rumors | date=2020-12-27 | url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2020/12/jordan-mcrae-signs-with-beijing-ducks.html | access-date=2025-10-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 27, 2020 |title=McRae signs contract with Beijing Ducks worth $1.5M |url=https://twitter.com/RealQuintonMayo/status/1343310085062320128 |website=Twitter.com}}</ref> He played seven games, in which he averaged 11.3 points, 1.3 assists, and 0.6 steals per game.<ref name="basketball.realgm.com" />

===Metropolitans 92 (2021–2022)===
On August 22, 2021, McRae signed with [[Metropolitans 92]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Skerletic |first=Dario |date=August 22, 2021 |title=Jordan McRae joins Metropolitans 92 |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jordan-mcrae-joins-metropolitans-92/ |access-date=August 22, 2021 |work=Sportando |language=En}}</ref> In 31 games he averaged 13.8 points,  2.5 assists, and 1.0 steals per game.<ref name="basketball.realgm.com" />

===Hapoel Tel Aviv (2022–2023)===
On September 23, 2022, he signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Skerletic |first=Dario |date=October 16, 2022 |title=Jordan McRae joins Hapoel Tel Aviv |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jordan-mcrae-joins-hapoel-tel-aviv/ |access-date=October 16, 2022 |work=Sportando |language=En}}</ref> In 47 games he averaged 15.7 points, 2.6 assists, and 1.0 steals  per game.<ref name="basketball.realgm.com" />

===AEK Athens (2023–2024)===
On July 14, 2023, he signed a one-year contract with [[Greek Basket League|GBL]] club [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Επίσημο: Στην ΑΕΚ ο Τζόρνταν ΜακΡέι! |url=https://www.sport-fm.gr/article/basket/greece/aek-anakoinwse-tzordan-makrei/4896950 |access-date=July 14, 2023 |website=sport-fm.gr |language=Greek |location=Online}}</ref> In 21 games he averaged 13.9 points, 2.2 assists,  and 0,9 steals  per game, while shooting .814 from the free throw line.<ref name=refe/>

===Scafati Basket (2024)===
On October 28, 2024, he signed with [[Scafati Basket]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/givova-scafati-signs-jordan-mcrae/|title=Givova Scafati signs Jordan McRae|date=October 28, 2024|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=October 28, 2024 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> In five games he averaged 3.8 points and 0.8 assists per game.<ref name=refe>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/players/jordan-mcrae-1.html "Jordan McRae International Stats,"] Basketball Reference.</ref>

===Hapoel Holon (2025–present)===
In the 2025–26 season, McRae played for [[Hapoel Holon B.C.|Hapoel Holon]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].  In 31 games he averaged 16.0 points, 2.2 assists, and 0.8 steals per game, while shooting .889 from the free throw line.<ref name=real>[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jordan-McRae/Summary/9345 "Jordan McRae,"] realgm.com.</ref>
